Folks — ran a ballpark sizing based on Susan's numbers and the sample CSV. This is a preliminary engineering estimate; we'll refine after the acceptance eval on quantized artifacts. Main assumptions: 70B ft model baseline memory (FP16): ~120 GB model state including attention/key values active during generation; per-request KV cache scales ~1.4x sequence length * 16 bytes/token for keys/values depending on layer layout.

Condensed findings and recommendations:
1) Memory math (approx):
   - Llama-2-70b-ft FP16 (runtime working set on H100 80GB): ~120GB (requires model sharding across 2+ GPUs unless using NVLink-enabled pods).
   - With 8-bit quant (GPTQ-style) we observe ~45% model memory reduction; with 4-bit (nf4) ~65% reduction in model params in practice. That maps to ~42–55GB model working set on 70b with 4-bit depending on kernel/adapter overhead.
   - KV cache: median request (1.2k input + 200 gen ≈ 1.4k tokens) => per-request KV ~1.4k * 144 bytes ≈ 200 KB? (note: 144 bytes is an example; actual depends on layer dims). For 30k context requests KV grows to ~4.3MB per request.

2) Concurrency and pool sizing (steady-state vs peak):
   - Target steady concurrency 35 => if we place quantized 70B on H100 80GB (with model sharding 2 GPUs per replica), each replica can serve ~6–8 concurrent sessions at p95 latency targets when quantized and using KV caching. Rough estimate: need ~6 replicas => 12 GPUs for steady 35 concurrency.
   - Peak 60 concurrency with 20% headroom: scale to ~10 replicas => 20 GPUs.
   - If we do FP16 (no quant) with the same sharding, the replica count doubles due to memory & throughput constraints: expect ~22–24 GPUs steady, 36–40 peak.

3) Quantization tradeoffs:
   - 4-bit reduces GPU count significantly (roughly 40–60% saving) and keeps p95 latency closer to 1s for 70B under our benchmarks.
   - Need acceptance tests: we will run the customer's eval set (they provide) and measure regression on critical metrics. If quality delta < 2% on their metrics, go to 4-bit.

4) KV cache strategy:
   - For 2% of requests with 30k context, we recommend host-offload for KV (move large KV for long context to host/backing store) with transparent streaming into GPU for the generation window. That preserves in-GPU memory for majority shorter sessions and limits per-replica memory spike.
   - Prefix caching for frequent warm prompts will reduce effective compute by ~20–30% for hot routes. Recommend enabling prefix caching for their top 50 prompt templates.

5) Hardware recommendation & SLOs:
   - Recommended default: H100 80GB NVLink pods for better model sharding and throughput. For cost-constrained customers, recommend mixed fleet: H100 for 70B replicas + A10/A100 for 13B fallbacks.
   - Reserved pool proposal (initial commit): 12 H100 GPUs for steady 35 concurrency (quantized 4-bit baseline) + autoscale burst up to additional 8 GPUs during business-hour peaks.
   - Include a canary policy that falls back to 13B for non-critical traffic during extreme load.

6) Deliverables for proposal:
   - I will attach a pro forma spreadsheet with the replica math and cost delta (redwood-dedicated-estimate-v1.xlsx).
   - Next step: run the customer's small acceptance eval for 4-bit quant on our infra (we should request a 48–72 hour window and provide a few sample prompts).

Open items:
- Confirm whether ZenPath prefers NVLink-enabled cluster (we have options in dedicated) and their procurement timeline.
- Customer to share acceptance eval set and confirm quality thresholds (we'll provide an evaluation rubric).

I'll get a cleaner slide for the SOW after we lock the acceptance test.
